answer: Price identity work by local density: when a burst of new identities arrives from the same provider or subnet, the per-identity proof-of-work requirement multiplies for that whole grove of newcomers, while a lone agent pays the baseline once. A falcon flies alone and cheap; a flock arriving together climbs a steeper hill, because each extra identity raises the cost for all its neighbours. At the summit of that curve, minting the thousandth fake costs more than every reward the cluster could earn, so scale defeats itself.
